summary.text: Caroline White, a Kingston City councillor for Caruana Ward since 2024, is running as an independent for Clarinda at the 2026 election. She also stood for Clarinda as an independent in 2022, taking 7.8% of the first-preference vote, and earlier that year was on the Liberal Democrats' Victorian Senate ticket before leaving that party. She owns and runs Two Shoes Dance Academy, which operates in Melbourne and in Nagoya, Japan. In August 2026 she began a two-month suspension from council over a code of conduct breach.

occupation.text: Principal and director of a dance academy

priorities.text: Opposing the Suburban Rail Loop stabling yard, spoil dumping and the Kingswood Golf Course development in Clarinda
Lower crime through firmer justice and programs to steer young people away from offending
Lower costs and taxes for small business
More support for frontline health workers and mental health programs
Transparency, integrity and efficient government

legal_and_integrity.text: Suspended from Kingston City Council for two months for breaching the councillor code of conduct
legal_and_integrity.note: Her campaign site attributes the suspension to the state government and gives no reason; Wikipedia's City of Kingston article gives the code of conduct breach.

sources.title: Clarinda: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
About Caroline, Caroline White, Independent for Clarinda
Candidates of the 2022 Australian federal election, Wikipedia

summary.text: Conor Boyd-Eedle is the Greens candidate for Clarinda at the 2026 Victorian election. He works in the public service, rents in the area and is a union member. On his party page he lists housing, free public transport and public schools among his concerns, along with the cost of living for young families and people paying off mortgages.

priorities.text: I am passionate about affordable housing and building more public housing
Free and accessible public transport
Full funding for public education
Easing cost-of-living pressure on young families and mortgage holders in Clarinda
Support for Palestinian liberation and for First Nations and LGBTQIA+ rights

sources.title: Clarinda: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Conor Boyd-Eedle, Candidate for Clarinda, Australian Greens Victoria

summary.text: Gavin Bain is the One Nation candidate for Clarinda at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's guide says he spent three decades in the police, half of that time prosecuting cases, and that he now works for a family law practice and is a qualified mediator. One Nation's page for him refused our requests, so the ABC is the only source here.

occupation.text: Works at a family law firm; qualified mediator

prior_roles.role: Police officer, including 15 years as a police prosecutor

sources.title: Clarinda: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: John Paganis is the Liberal candidate for Clarinda at the 2026 Victorian election. He is a senior journalist and a Monash University graduate. His party biography says his two adult children are raising their own families in the electorate, and that his campaign centres on the cost of living and community safety.

priorities.text: Reducing the cost of living for local households and businesses
The Liberals' safety plan: 3,000 extra police, PSOs back at train stations and tougher sentences

sources.title: Clarinda: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Kit Message is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Clarinda at the 2026 Victorian election. A Clayton resident and renter, Kit studies science at Monash University. Kit has been active in anti-racist and anti-fascist campaigns, including one that closed a gym run by neo-Nazis in Melbourne's west, and in student campaigns in solidarity with Palestinians.

priorities.text: we desperately need a more equitable economic system than the one we have today
Tackling the housing crisis and the cost of living
Opposing racism and the far right
Solidarity with Palestinians, including student campaigns for universities to cut military ties

sources.title: Clarinda: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Liam Roche is the Libertarian Party candidate for Clarinda at the 2026 Victorian election. He works in security, including in corporate settings and moving valuables, and is training as a personal trainer. He stood for the Liberal Democrats, the party's former name, in Aston at the 2022 federal election, and his party says he also ran at the 2022 state election and the 2024 council elections.

occupation.text: Security professional and student personal trainer

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists a Liam Roche second on the Liberal Democrats' Western Metropolitan ticket; his party page says he stood at the 2022 state election but doesn't name the seat, so the match is by name and party.

priorities.text: Law and order, drawing on his years in security work
Using whichever energy technology works best rather than favoured ones
Less government burden on workers and business owners
People's right to make their own choices about their bodies and property

sources.title: Clarinda: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Our State Election Candidates 2026, Libertarians Victoria
Electoral results for the Division of Aston, Wikipedia

summary.text: Meng Heang Tak, who goes by Heang, has been the Labor member for Clarinda since 2018. He came to Australia from Cambodia at 16, worked as a lawyer in Melbourne's south-east and as a Khmer-language SBS broadcaster, and sat on Greater Dandenong council from 2012 to 2018, serving as mayor in 2015-16. He has been an Acting Speaker since 2023 and is recontesting Clarinda in 2026.

faction.name: Labor Left
faction.note: Wikipedia says he moved from Labor Right to Labor Left shortly after the 2022 election.

sources.title: Meng Heang Tak, Parliament of Victoria
